evidence.claim: Card baseline over 180 days: 48 transactions, 100% online, 100% product C, mean $39.80, std $25.21, max $94.70 - the disputed $59.67 (amount_z 0.79, 1.5x mean) is ordinary for this card.

The card already used 13 distinct devices in 180 days (top device only 16/48 txns), so the 'New' flag on 'Windows | unknown | edge 16.0 | unknown' is weak evidence of compromise on this particular account.
Episode window contains exactly one transaction (3534820) - no 2-4 transaction burst, no card-testing run (<$5 authorizations), no just-under-$500 run, no region change (new_region_for_card false).
Model risk score on the flagged transaction is 0.37 - low, and by policy a score is a reason to look, not a verdict.
An identical $59.67 charge exists two months earlier (3368735, 2016-10); looks_monthly is false with only one prior instance, so it is a partial, not a confirmed, recurring pattern.

The only rare shared device (SAMSUNG SM-A310F ... samsung browser 6.4; 6 cards all-time, 2 in window) is NOT the device used on the flagged transaction, and the single card it links to (C03938-K1, 7 txns, $356.52) has no confirmed fraud cases - no shared-origin evidence under R6.

Memory holds 10 device-linked confirmed-fraud cases (8 card_not_present_new_device, 2 card_not_present_fraud, e.g. CC-2898 $209.28, CC-2675 $87.85), showing this bank does see new-device CNP fraud at similar small amounts - the reason the case is not dismissed outright.

Semantically similar closed cases CC-0189 and CC-0986 were cleared after the cardholder confirmed a purchase from a new phone/device, supporting that a lone New-device flag frequently resolves as legitimate.
Policy R1 requires verification rather than a block when the case rests on a single signal and probability is under 0.70.
Customer validation: the cardholder recognises the identical October charge as their own recurring merchant billing and accepts the December charge as the same subscription.

case.summary: Customer C09988 disputed a $59.67 online charge (3534820, 2016-12-11) on card C09988-K1. The transaction matches the card's exclusively online, product-C profile and is only 0.79 SD above a $39.80 mean, well under the $94.70 historical max; the model scored it 0.37. The sole anomaly is a 'New' device flag, but the card has used 13 devices in 180 days, and the rare shared device in the graph is a different device linked to one card with no confirmed fraud. A prior identical $59.67 charge (3368735, October) suggests a forgotten recurring merchant billing. Verification was requested under R1; on the assumed confirmation the alert resolves as legitimate, with a case record kept and the customer warned to re-contact if further unrecognised charges appear.

evidence_requests.assumed_response: Customer, when shown the identical $59.67 charge from 2016-10 (txn 3368735) at the same merchant, recognises it as their own recurring subscription and accepts that the 2016-12-11 charge is the same subscription billed from a browser they recently started using.

initial.reason: R1: p=0.45 is not decisive; verify before any block
§3a: a case is opened whenever evidence is requested

final.reason: §3a: every customer dispute opens a case
R3: close the alert as legitimate and note the confirmation

next_best_actions.what_changed: Before verification the case was genuinely balanced at 0.45 (dispute plus a New-device flag against a fully in-profile amount and channel); the customer recognising the identical October charge as their own recurring billing moved the assessment to legitimate at 0.30.

sar.reason: No report: activity assessed as legitimate (R3); §3a filing conditions do not apply.

stop_reason: The verification response settles the question and exposure is only $59.67, well under the $500 escalation threshold; no further graph steps (no burst, no region change, no fraud-bearing device link) would change the decision.
